title: This Country Song Just Broke a Huge Chart Record
summary:
Have you ever had a song stuck in your head for weeks? Imagine if the whole country couldn't stop listening to it for 23 weeks! That's what happened with Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas.' It just became the longest-running No. 1 hit in Billboard Hot 100 history.

The song is a sad, twangy country tune about losing a guy to a pretty stranger. It even mentions the classic song 'Amarillo by Morning.' NPR says it's 'catchy as all get out' and feels like it could have been a hit any time in the past 50 years.

So why can't anyone knock it off the top? One big reason: country fans have moved from radio to streaming. They play the song over and over, and the charts count every listen. Also, 2026 has been a weak year for pop music. Some big pop stars released albums that didn't make a huge splash.

There's also just so much music out there. With millions of songs available, people — and radio programmers — stick to the hits they already know. And 'Choosin' Texas' still sells thousands of copies each week.

Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' might take back the record in December. But for now, Ella Langley is the queen of the charts.
why_it_matters: It shows how the songs you stream in your headphones every day can actually change the charts — and that a song someone loves can quietly make history.

background_read: The Billboard Hot 100 is a chart made by Billboard magazine that ranks songs using radio plays, sales and streaming in the United States.
Mariah Carey is a famous American singer, and her Christmas song has gone back to No. 1 in December many times because people play it every holiday season.
Country music, a style from the American South with guitars and fiddles, has become one of the biggest kinds of music on streaming services.
Article_Structure: WHO: Country singer Ella Langley, whose song 'Choosin' Texas' set the record — and Mariah Carey, whose Christmas song might take it back.
WHAT: 'Choosin' Texas' became the longest-running No. 1 hit in Billboard Hot 100 history, staying on top for 23 weeks.
WHERE: On the U.S. music charts, driven by streaming services and country radio.
WHY: Fans can replay songs endlessly on streaming (and every listen counts), country listeners have moved from radio to streaming, and 2026 was a weak year for pop, so nothing knocked it off the top.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled that a country song is getting this much attention and that it set a record that pop stars usually hold.
Some say the record partly comes from the way charts count endless streaming, not just from how many people truly love the song.
They point out that a weak year for pop music plus changes in how people listen can keep one hit on top far longer than it could in the past.
